name: Grimand's Armor
summary: In Stormwind, Grimand's Armor takes shape through a test of Furen Longbeard's methods. Grimand Elmore crafts a helm from rare materials, meant to endure punishing blows in battle. For an Alliance warrior, it marks a step toward mastery.

sections.title: A Master's Innovation Proven
sections.body: Grimand Elmore tests Furen Longbeard's daring smithing methods at his forge in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Grimand had doubted the dwarven master armorer's theories. To put them to the test, a warrior gathers rare elemental and beast components in hostile territory and brings them to Grimand. He uses the materials to forge a reinforced helm built to endure crushing impacts.

sections.title: Forging the Aegis
sections.body: Grimand's finished coif shows that Furen's metallurgic insights were sound. He treats the metal to withstand pressure and physical blows that would warp ordinary steel. Grimand gives the coif to the warrior who helped him, honoring Furen's craft and the warrior's resolve. The armor can help them hold the frontline against Azeroth's greatest threats.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
faq.answer: Grimand Elmore finishes a specially treated coif with the rare materials you gathered, testing Furen Longbeard's experimental smithing methods. This is the final handoff in a major warrior training line.
Grimand Elmore is a skilled dwarven weaponsmith in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He works with colleagues in Ironforge to help rising warriors obtain specialized armor.

faq.q: Who is Furen Longbeard and why is he mentioned?
faq.answer: Furen Longbeard is a dwarven master armorer in Stormwind's Dwarven District. He devised a method to fortify armor against immense stress, but Grimand doubted his claims until you brought materials to test it.

faq.q: What quest leads directly into this one?
faq.answer: This follows 'Burning Blood'. There, the warrior brings Grimand the final rare reagent, Burning Blood from the Nightbane worgen of Roland's Doom in Duskwood, so he can quench and temper the metal.

faq.q: Can any class complete this quest?
faq.answer: No. This chain is for Alliance warriors around their thirtieth season, and marks a rite of passage toward durable mail armor.

faq.q: Where does this turn-in take place?
faq.answer: You bring the coif to Grimand Elmore at his anvil in Stormwind City's Dwarven District.

angles.text: As an Alliance warrior, you reach a defining step in your training: a resilient coif forged to withstand the hard blows of frontline combat.
The exchange brings together two dwarven smiths in Stormwind's Dwarven District, using unusual reagents to temper metal.
Grimand Elmore draws on Furen Longbeard's designs, as the dwarven smiths of Stormwind's Dwarven District pool discoveries to arm Alliance warriors.
